findings.issue: Step 1 still uses an 'or' construction: 'Verify the project still compiles after removal but before adding the new file (or edit both in the same change set).' This makes atomic change optional. If a developer removes the placeholder in one step and the real class has not been added yet, the project will not compile. The word 'or' allows the non-atomic path.
findings.fix: Remove the 'or edit both in the same change set' alternative entirely. Mandate the atomic approach as the only option: 'Always remove the placeholder and create InsightSession.swift as a single atomic change. Do not remove the placeholder as a separate compilation step.'

findings.issue: Step 10 (handleStreamError) only says 'Distinguish Task.isCancelled (silent) from real errors.' It does not mention AIProviderError.streamingError, which is introduced by Task 1 as the specific case thrown by streamCompletion for SSE error events and oversized lines. A developer implementing step 10 without cross-reading Task 1 will not know to explicitly pattern-match streamingError vs httpError vs parseError and may accidentally treat streamingError as retryable when it should not always be.
findings.fix: Add to step 10: 'Pattern-match AIProviderError cases explicitly: .streamingError — set lastError, retryable=true (API-side error, worth retrying); .httpError — set lastError, retryable depends on status (429/5xx retryable, 4xx not); Task.isCancelled / CancellationError — silent, no lastError. Use a typed switch rather than relying solely on localizedDescription.'

findings.issue: Task 5 defines the JS window function as 'window.setInsightView(snapshotJSON)' (step 10, acceptance criteria). Task 6 calls 'window.loadInsightView(<json>)' (step 1, description, smoke test). These are different names. The Swift bridge method in Task 6 is named loadInsightView and it calls window.loadInsightView — but the JS function Task 5 will implement is window.setInsightView. At runtime the JS call from Swift will throw ReferenceError because window.loadInsightView is undefined.
findings.fix: Align the JS function name in both tasks. Choose one name and apply it consistently. Options: (a) rename Task 5's window.setInsightView to window.loadInsightView everywhere in tasks/5.md; OR (b) rename Task 6's bridge method call target from window.loadInsightView to window.setInsightView everywhere in tasks/6.md. The tech-spec (line 570) names the Swift method loadInsightView(snapshot:into:) but does not specify the JS function name — so either direction is valid, but both tasks must agree.

findings.issue: Step 8 says 'call mermaid.render (or mermaid.run({ nodes: [singleNode] })) on each block.' mermaid.render is the old v9 API that takes (id, definition) and returns SVG via a callback/promise — it has a completely different calling convention. mermaid.run is the correct v10+ API and matches what the existing codebase uses at L1247 of index.html. Listing mermaid.render first is misleading and will cause a developer to use the wrong API.
findings.fix: Remove 'mermaid.render (or ...)' from step 8. Replace with: 'call mermaid.run({ nodes: [singleNode] }) on each block individually' — matching the existing codebase pattern at L1247 of index.html and the implementation hint at line 150 of this task.

findings.issue: The init signature is init(folderURL:mdFiles:providerClient:graphRAG:) with graphRAG as non-optional. However, graphRAG.mapReduceForFolder is only needed when mdFiles.count > 30. There is no guidance on what to do if graphRAG is nil but mdFiles.count > 30. Since graphRAG is non-optional in the init, this is not a critical issue, but the edge-case section and step 4 should clarify that the caller (Task 7 WorkspaceManager) is responsible for always providing a non-nil graphRAG instance when creating InsightSession.
findings.fix: Add to the edge cases section: 'graphRAG is always non-optional — WorkspaceManager (Task 7) must provide a valid GraphRAG instance at InsightSession creation time. InsightSession does not need to guard against nil graphRAG.'
